question.problem:
Solve the linear congruence $3x≡3\,(\text{mod}\,4)$ using trial and error. Express your answer as a nonnegative integer smaller than $4.$

$x≡$
{{field-1}}$\,(\text{mod}\,4)$
question.worked_solution:
Since the modulus $n=4$ is fairly small, we can solve the congruence by trial and error. 

Substituting $x=0,1,2,3$ into the congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot 0 & ≡0≢3 &  & (\text{mod}\,4) &  & \times  \\ 3\cdot 1 & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,4) &  & ✓ \\ 3\cdot 2 & ≡6≡1\cdot 4+2≡2≢3 &  & (\text{mod}\,4) &  & \times  \\ 3\cdot 3 & ≡9≡2\cdot 4+1≡1≢3 &  & (\text{mod}\,4) &  & \times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,4).$

**Note**: Any number congruent to $1$ modulo $4$ is a solution. For example, note that $5≡1,$ and this also satisfies our congruence:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & ≡3\cdot 5\, &  & (\text{mod}\,4) \\  & ≡15\, &  & (\text{mod}\,4) \\  & ≡3\cdot 4+3\, &  & (\text{mod}\,4) \\  & ≡0+3\, &  & (\text{mod}\,4) \\  & ≡3\,\,✓\, &  & (\text{mod}\,4)\end{aligned}
$$
